fields.title: S2U1Q1
fields.description: Given a class where age is assigned on the class, not on self, what happens if you create two people and then change one person’s age?
fields.explanation:
Class attributes are shared across all instances. Updating it via any instance affects all.
The correct answer is: All Person objects reflect the changed age, because it is a class (static) attribute.

fields.title: S2U1Q2
fields.description: In the example with a Canvas class that holds a list of shapes and calls describe() on each, what requirement must any object meet to be added to the canvas?
fields.explanation:
The Canvas calls shape.describe() for each stored object. Any shape added should therefore provide a describe() method.
The correct answer is: It must implement a describe() method that the canvas can call.

fields.title: S2U1Q3
fields.description: In Python classes, what is the main role of the __init__ method?
fields.explanation:
__init__ is the constructor that runs when you create an object and typically assigns initial values to instance attributes. It doesn’t return the object; the instance is created before __init__ runs.
The correct answer is: It runs automatically when the object is created and initializes instance attributes.

fields.title: S2U1Q4
fields.description: Which line correctly assigns a constructor parameter radius to an instance attribute in Python?
fields.explanation:
Inside instance methods, use self to refer to the current object. For example: self.radius = radius.
The correct answer is: self.radius = radius

fields.title: S2U1Q5
fields.description: Consider a class with a method defined as @staticmethod. Why can we call it as Adding.addingMethod(3, 4) without creating an instance?
fields.explanation:
@staticmethod declares a function that does not receive self or cls, so it can be invoked on the class without making an object.
The correct answer is: Because a static method does not require self and can be called on the class directly.
